newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan beats China in diplomatic tussle over Liberia.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan beats China in diplomatic tussle over Liberia.

text.p: Taiwan has won the latest battle in Beijing's war to keep Taipei isolated by securing diplomatic recognition from war-torn Liberia, Taipei officials said on Wednesday.

"Liberia recalled its ambassador posted by one of its warring factions in Beijing and sent an ambassador to Taipei on January 28 to open an embassy in our country," a Taiwan foreign ministry official told Reuters.
Charles Taylor, member of the Collective Presidency of Liberia, was expected to arrive in Taiwan on Thursday on a four-day official visit, the foreign ministry said.
The visit "represents firm relations between the two countries," Foreign Minister John Chang told reporters on Wednesday.
After a storm of protest from other members of Liberia's collective ruling council, interim head of state Ruth Perry ruled Taylor's nomination of the envoy as out of order.
Taylor argued he acted in line with power-sharing accords under which other council members had named key envoys. Perry has not said what she intends to do.

Taylor launched Liberia's civil war with an invasion from neighbouring Ivory Coast in late 1989. He has announced his plan to run in May 30 presidential elections which will formally bring an end to the divided Liberia government.
Liberia's decision ends an awkward diplomatic situation in which the war-torn West African country recognised both Taipei and its archrival Beijing.

China refuses to maintain ties with any country that recognises Taiwan. The two were split after a civil war ended in 1949, but Beijing still regards the island as a renegade province to be unified eventually with the mainland.
China has warned other countries against forging ties with Taipei and blocked efforts by the island to gain international recognition.
However China set up an embassy in Monrovia in 1993 despite the presence of Taipei's embassy there, apparently willing to show flexibility because of Liberia's domestic turmoil.
Liberia resumed official relations with Taiwan in October 1989 but has been unable to open its Taipei embassy until now because of the civil war, Taiwan ministry officials said.
Liberia's presidential and parliamentary elections will be held under a peace deal brokered by its neighbours last August to end seven years of civil war.
Well over 150,000 people, many of them civilians, have been killed in the fighting.
Taiwan and China started pushing hard for a Liberian decision late last year, as soon as peace came in sight.

A diplomatic source told Reuters that Taipei emerged victorious in the diplomacy struggle after promising to help in agricultural and other areas of development. "Taiwan has agreed to donate rice and help Liberia carry out reconstruction and other development projects," the source said.
Taiwan now has only 30 diplomatic allies, including South Africa which has expressed its intention to switch diplomatic recognition to Beijing at the end of this year.
